implementation_notes: The dominant Java realization: annotate the domain class @Entity and mark one property @Id (or @EmbeddedId) so the persistence provider owns identity and the persistence context acts as an identity map, returning one managed instance per primary key. Write equals/hashCode yourself along the documented guidance for generated ids: use a business or natural key that is set in the constructor, or compare by id only when the id is non-null with a stable class-based hashCode. If the entity will live in hash-based collections before it is persisted, assign the id early (UUID in the constructor) instead of relying on a database-generated key.
pitfalls: A @GeneratedValue id is null until flush, so equals/hashCode based on the id makes transient entities equal to everything or to nothing and changes the hash after persistence, corrupting sets and caches.
Hibernate proxies are subclasses: an equals that requires getClass() == other.getClass() fails for proxies, and field access on lazy state triggers loading; compare ids on the interface instead.
Lombok @Data / @EqualsAndHashCode generates attribute equality over all fields, which is the wrong semantics for an entity.

variants.name: Persistence-ignorant POJO with hand-written identity and a data mapper
variants.idiom_name: plain class with a final id assigned in the constructor and equals/hashCode by id
variants.implementation_notes: The DDD-strict realization keeps the entity a plain object with no persistence annotations: a final (or never-reassigned) id assigned at construction - typically UUID.randomUUID() or a typed identity value object - and equals/hashCode derived from that id only, while the inherited Object.equals already provides reference equality whenever one instance per identity is guaranteed in memory. Persistence is delegated to a data mapper and repository, so the model never sees JPA. Choose it when the domain model is the primary artifact and the mapping layer should stay replaceable; choose the JPA variant when the framework's identity map, lazy loading and change detection are wanted.
pitfalls: Without the framework's identity map, loading the same row twice creates two equal but distinct objects; the unit of work or repository must keep one instance per identity if edits must not diverge.

If the id is generated by the database, a plain POJO has no identity until after insert and cannot safely be used as a map key; generate the id client-side or assign it in the repository before the object is shared.
